source_text: Ὅτι οὐ δεῖ ἐν ταῖς κώμαις καὶ ἐν ταῖς χώραις καθίστασθαι ἐπισκόπους, ἀλλὰ περιοδευτάς· τοὺς μέν τοι ἤδη προκατασταθέντας, μηδὲν πράττειν ἄνευ γνώμης τοῦ ἐπισκόπου τοῦ ἐν τῇ πόλει· ὡσαύτως δὲ καὶ τοὺς πρεσβυτέρους μηδὲν πράττειν ἄνευ τῆς γνώμης τοῦ ἐπισκόπου.
thought_title: No bishops in villages; circuit visitors instead
orientation: The Council of Laodicea is issuing its own decrees, and this canon regulates rural church order.
pass_a_gloss: That it is not necessary to appoint bishops in the villages and in the country districts, but circuit visitors; but those already appointed beforehand, to do nothing without the judgment of the bishop in the city; and likewise also the presbyters to do nothing without the judgment of the bishop.

choices.why: The glossary fixes this rendering for the rural overseers appointed instead of resident bishops.
Renders the bishop's authoritative decision or approval, keeping the sense of consent required for action.
Preserves the absolute prohibition with the negative pronoun, matching the canon's force.
Keeps the impersonal δεῖ construction and the introductory Ὅτι that marks the canon's decree.

pass_b_english: Bishops are not to be appointed in villages and country districts, but circuit visitors instead. Those already appointed beforehand are to do nothing without the judgment of the bishop in the city. Likewise, presbyters are to do nothing without the judgment of the bishop.
